# Design quality

The archetype defines visual identity, not a page template. Compose for the company, content and task; there is no fixed section count, split ratio, card quota or mandatory component inventory. Keep recognizable type, imagery and material choices while inventing useful structures.

## The art of reduction

Keep only what helps someone understand, decide, act or recognize the identity. Explore freely, then make a deliberate editing pass: remove repeated messages, competing emphasis, redundant containers, unnecessary labels and decoration without a clear role. Let the necessary content speak through fewer stronger gestures, clear hierarchy and generous breathing room.

Reduction is a judgment about purpose, not a demand for sparse layouts or less functionality. Preserve useful detail, essential controls, expressive typography and the imagery or material that makes this identity distinctive. Group related information before hiding it; reveal secondary detail when needed without concealing critical context. A rich composition can be coherent when each part earns its place.

Give each view a clear center of attention. Supporting elements should explain, enable or enrich it rather than ask for equal attention. Use whitespace to separate ideas and pace the reading, not to stretch a thin page. Before finishing, ask of every element: what becomes harder to understand or do if this disappears? Remove it, merge it or quiet it when the answer is nothing. Inspect the resulting composition again; stop when further subtraction would damage meaning, usability or character.

## Hierarchy and breathing room

Make the key statement, selected object or important working value unmistakable through scale, weight, position and contrast. Give supporting copy a quieter readable role and associate labels with values and units. Use deliberate line breaks, optical spacing and actual loaded font styles. Expressive faces belong to display or short annotations; functional text stays clear.

Create whitespace through margins, padding, readable measures and coherent grouping. Keep useful complexity, diagrams and controls. Rich and quiet regions can alternate without deleting information or stretching empty sections. Preserve complete words, relevant content and an unambiguous reading order through overlap and cropping.

## Platform and task

Websites open with a dominant large image and a strong statement composed together on one continuous hero stage. The image establishes the story above the fold, and native type and controls complete it. Do not divide the hero into a standalone copy column beside a separate rectangular photograph or product card. This website rule takes precedence over any archetype example suggesting that arrangement; it does not constrain application working surfaces or later website sections.

Art-direct the stage for the subject and identity: an expansive photograph with a quiet region for type; an oversized object with its background removed on a solid or gradient ground; or a large illustrative scene with the statement integrated into it. The statement can overlap the image or occupy a deliberate band above it, but the image must remain a commanding part of the opening. Make room for the type through framing, negative space, selective lighting or a subtle continuous tonal treatment. Avoid a visible dark rectangle behind copy. Keep navigation restrained, the primary action obvious and the subject recognizable. Recompose the crop and type on narrow screens rather than shrinking a desktop split. Later content follows its purpose and finishes coherently.

Mobile apps recompose the real task with safe areas, refined hierarchy, touch-sized controls, explicit selection, confirmation and next-state feedback. Keep relevant secondary actions and persistent navigation visible. Web apps organize navigation, working surface, controls and selected context around the workflow: a console, editor, map, queue or dashboard should work as that product.

Use supplied facts as the complete dataset. Do not invent measurements, analytical series, claims or completed operational states. Where a sample state is necessary, make it clearly illustrative; keep confirmation before committing actions. Build interface text, controls, diagrams and charts as editable native elements, not generated screenshots.

## Art direction and materials

For each image, define its narrative role, literal subject, viewpoint, light, materials, crop and quiet regions for type. Dithering, noir, selective color, film-inspired grading and shaders are optional image treatments with a specific purpose. Protect the subject and readable information; effects never stand in for art direction.

## Color relationships

Honor explicitly selected fonts, shape and elevation presets. Choose final colors for the company, content, imagery and task. Named color palettes and their hex values are optional references, including when supplied by a style preset; freely replace part or all of them for a stronger identity. Only colors directly required by the user or supplied brand guidelines are constraints. Historical palette names do not prescribe a hue.

Define a dominant ground and distinguish working surfaces through lightness and contrast. Establish readable primary, supporting and inverse text; a recognizable action and selection color; quiet boundaries; and separate, consistently labeled status colors. Decide where chroma belongs and how much area it occupies. A neutral ground with a vivid accent, a dark field with luminous detail or a saturated ground with contrasting type are possible relationships, not mandatory recipes. Keep these roles coherent across the interface and check contrast on the actual image, translucent surface or fill.

Do not use beige, cream, ivory, tan or warm off-white for interface backgrounds or container fills. Choose deliberate color, pure white, cool neutrals or dark grounds instead. Craft, warmth and luxury can come from type, light, texture and imagery without a beige canvas. Natural material colors in photography are unaffected.

Never use harsh shadows. Surfaces may be flat, subtly elevated or lifted by a broad softly diffused shadow. Use low opacity and generous blur; avoid hard offset blocks, sharp cast edges, heavy dark rims and shadowed text. Tactile, glass and collage directions obey the same rule. Depth alone never communicates interaction state.

Inspect the actual render at its intended size: hierarchy, font loading, crop, contrast, spacing, clipping, useful actions and state clarity. Record image or font limitations outside the product UI.
